participant_roles: Originator=dashboard (writable store); Memento=history (string array store of serialized JSON); Caretaker=HistoryButtons.svelte; Caretaker/Index=historyIndex (writable store); Registration=historyUpdater (function); Invoker=record (writable store)
intent_and_evidence: The classic dashboard requires undo/redo capabilities when users modify dashboard views, sections, or cards. The originator state is held in the $dashboard store. When edits occur, modal dialogs invoke $record(), executing the snapshot callback registered via historyUpdater() (HistoryButtons.svelte:18). snapshot() serializes $dashboard via JSON.stringify and appends it to $history while tracking $historyIndex (HistoryButtons.svelte:43-55). When undo/redo is triggered via buttons or Ctrl/Cmd+Z, set(newIndex) restores state by parsing JSON.parse($history[$historyIndex]) back into $dashboard (HistoryButtons.svelte:75-82). This fulfills the Memento pattern intent by externalizing and restoring state snapshots without exposing internal object mutations.

participant_roles: Originator=hearthConfig (writable store); Memento=HearthConfig (interface); Caretaker/Storage=undoStack, redoStack, editSnapshot; Caretaker/Mutator=updateConfig; Caretaker/Undo=undoConfig; Caretaker/Redo=redoConfig; Caretaker/Transaction=enterEditMode, cancelEdit
intent_and_evidence: The Hearth dashboard UI manages its own configuration lifecycle independent of the classic dashboard. updateConfig() pushes the current HearthConfig onto undoStack (capped at 50 entries) before applying a mutator to a structuredClone (store.ts:43-53). undoConfig() and redoConfig() transfer full configuration snapshots between undoStack and redoStack, restoring the active state into hearthConfig (store.ts:55-69). Furthermore, entering edit mode captures a separate transaction memento editSnapshot, allowing cancelEdit() to roll back all intermediate edits unconditionally (store.ts:94-110). This is an independent Memento implementation with both stack-based undo/redo and transactional rollback.

participant_roles: Originator/Caretaker=KonvaEditor (class); Memento=KonvaHistory (interface); Caretaker/Storage=undoStack, redoStack (arrays); Snapshot-Creator=KonvaEditor.record; Caretaker/Undo=KonvaEditor.undo; Caretaker/Redo=KonvaEditor.redo; Restorer=KonvaEditor.applyState
intent_and_evidence: The Picture Elements floorplan canvas editor requires undo/redo of geometric shapes, icons, and selection states. KonvaEditor maintains private undoStack and redoStack storing KonvaHistory objects (containing element descriptors and selected shape IDs). record() captures the current layer state and pushes it onto undoStack if different from previous state (konvaEditor.ts:754-775). undo() and redo() transfer mementos between the stacks and delegate to applyState() to reconcile, add, or destroy Konva shapes on the active layer (konvaEditor.ts:780-840). This satisfies Memento intent within an OOP class architecture, where Originator and Caretaker are co-located in KonvaEditor.

participant_roles: Component=Section (interface); Composite=horizontal-stack, vertical-stack Sections (sections array); Leaf=Leaf Section (items array); Leaf-Element=Item (union type); Client=findInSections (function); Client/Caller=getSelected (function)
source_locations: Component=src/lib/Types.ts:45-56; Composite=src/lib/Types.ts:53-55; Leaf=src/lib/Types.ts:48-48; Leaf-Element=src/lib/Types.ts:42-43; Client=src/lib/Utils.ts:44-60; Client/Caller=src/lib/Utils.ts:25-42
intent_and_evidence: Dashboard view layouts form a recursive part-whole composition. A Section interface defines both leaf sections containing UI cards (items: Item[]) and composite stack sections (horizontal-stack or vertical-stack) containing nested child sections (sections: Section[]). findInSections() recursively traverses composite sections and searches child items uniformly without requiring client code to differentiate between top-level sections and nested stacks (Utils.ts:44-60). getSelected() leverages this recursive traversal to look up components across the entire layout tree (Utils.ts:25-42).

participant_roles: Component=Condition (interface); Composite=and, or Conditions (conditions array); Leaf=state, numeric_state, screen Conditions; Uniform-Operation=validateCondition (function); Composite-Handler=handleAnd, handleOr; Leaf-Handler=handleState, handleNumericState, handleScreen; Client=handleAllConditions
intent_and_evidence: Section visibility in dashboards is governed by recursive conditional expressions. Condition defines a unified tree structure where leaf conditions evaluate entity state, numeric thresholds, or media queries, while composite conditions (and, or) contain nested conditions: Condition[]. validateCondition() provides uniform dispatch across all condition types (Conditional.ts:70-90). handleAnd() and handleOr() recurse on child conditions using validateCondition() (Conditional.ts:132-163), allowing arbitrary Boolean trees to be evaluated uniformly by client handleAllConditions() (Conditional.ts:58-65). In functional TypeScript idioms, free functions replace polymorphic class methods.

participant_roles: Subject=conn (Connection object); Subscription-Function=subscribeEntities (function); ConcreteObserver=states (writable store); Observer-Client=Reactive UI Components ($states subscribers)
intent_and_evidence: The dashboard requires live, asynchronous synchronization with external Home Assistant smart home entity state changes over WebSockets. Upon establishing connection conn, subscribeEntities() registers an observer callback that pushes updated entity maps into the Svelte states store (Socket.ts:116). Svelte components throughout the application subscribe to $states, automatically re-rendering corresponding tiles, cards, and sensor readouts upon state notification without polling.

intent_and_evidence: Client components display diverse entity types (lights, switches, sensors, cameras, climate units) and need to open domain-specific detailed configuration and control dialogs without hardcoding modal component bindings. openEntityModal() inspects the entity_id via getDomain() and dynamically imports and instantiates the appropriate modal component (e.g. LightModal for light, SwitchModal for switch/remote/siren, SensorModal for sensors/weather, CalendarModal for calendars) via openModal() (modals.ts:11-171). This encapsulates product creation behind a parameterized factory interface.

intent_and_evidence: Picture Elements floorplans require both a lightweight display mode (KonvaViewer) and a rich interactive designer (KonvaEditor). KonvaBase defines the skeleton structure for canvas initialization, stage binding, viewport scaling, DPI adjustment, and SVG/XML rendering (konvaBase.ts:13-518). KonvaBase defines hooks such as updateCallback() which KonvaEditor overrides to coordinate toolbar and inspector synchronization (konvaBase.ts:53-55). Subclasses KonvaViewer and KonvaEditor reuse the foundational canvas lifecycle while specializing behavior for passive display versus interactive shape transformation.
